articles.title: U.S. intelligence warns Iranian plots to kill Americans are in 'advanced stages'
articles.summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Friday that Iran has "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel" abroad, with plots to kill Americans reaching "advanced stages" in the Middle East and other countries. The warning, contained in an unclassified memo that was sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and obtained by CBS News, comes as the State Department adjusts staffing at diplomatic posts across the Middle East , and the U.S. military pares back its footprint in the region, amid concerns about direct threats from Iran and threats from the Iranian-backed Houthi movement in Yemen. "The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries," Clayton wrote. The memo, which was issued as the Trump administration weighs resuming military strikes against Iran, does not identify specific targets or countries where the alleged plots are underway, or indicate whether attacks may be imminent. Clayton said the U.S. intelligence community is working to downgrade sensitive intelligence — received through various channels — so it can be shared more broadly with State Department personnel. CIA Director John Ratcliffe was copied on the memo. Axios was first to report on the memo. The warning follows a series of precautions at U.S. diplomatic facilities across the region. Earlier this week, the State Department ordered non-essential U.S. embassy personnel and their families to depart Saudi Arabia. Several other American embassies in the region adjusted their staffing under "restricted operations" status, which allows them to reduce the number of personnel without formally going on ordered departure, CBS News previously reported. "When it comes to our staffing at embassies, we constantly evaluate new information about the security environment," a U.S. official told CBS News on Friday. "The threat of Houthi attacks and of Iranian terror plots targeting U.S. officials are informing our decisions on staffing adjustments for embassies on RO [Restricted Operations] Status in the region." A U.S. official and a senior U.S. military official also told CBS News this week that the military has been quietly reducing its footprint at posts in the Middle East due to ongoing threats. Houthi militants have stepped up drone and missile attacks against Saudi Arabia, targeting oil infrastructure and airports. One strike on Riyadh's King Khalid Airport earlier this month killed at least a dozen people , including a U.S. citizen, and injured hundreds more. Last weekend, U.S. embassies in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and other countries warned Americans to exercise caution due to Houthi attacks. Although the U.S. and Iran have refrained from striking each other in recent weeks, President Trump has not ruled out restarting hostilities after next month's midterm elections. Iran has also continued to take responsibility for attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. At a campaign rally in Florida on Friday, Mr. Trump suggested the U.S. could launch another operation against Iran if Tehran failed to reach an agreement. "We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree," the president said, invoking the name of the U.S. military campaign launched in February. articles.title: DOJ gives California counties 48 hours to help identify suspected noncitizen voters
articles.summary: Los Angeles (AP) — Federal prosecutors sent letters to county registrars across California on Friday demanding that local officials set aside and verify ballots that the Department of Justice said may belong to noncitizens , according to the Los Angeles County registrar and a letter obtained by The Associated Press. The letters are the latest escalation in a legal battle between California and President Donald Trump's Department of Justice, which has recently focused on the state in its efforts to root out noncitizen voting ahead of the midterm elections. Data shows illegal voting by people who aren't U.S. citizens is incredibly rare , difficult to prove and has not been shown to change the outcome of races. Earlier this month, the federal government targeted Los Angeles County and the California Secretary of State's office in a lawsuit that aimed to block them from counting the votes of roughly 20,000 people who are “likely” noncitizen voters. A hearing on the case is scheduled for Tuesday. The Trump administration asked the 9th Circuit court of appeals to rule on the lawsuit barring a decision from the district judge assigned to the case. They set a deadline for Saturday. Now, according to the LA County registrar’s office, at least 18 counties across the state have received similar letters. They have been given a 48 hour deadline to provide identifying information corresponding with ballots that the federal government believes were sent to noncitizens illegally registered to vote. The letter requests that county officials also sequester any ballots where citizenship cannot be verified. “Any election official who knowingly processes the ballot of a noncitizen is opening themselves to legal jeopardy," said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli. The Justice Department is asking counties to send information about the voters it suspects are noncitizens including social security numbers, ID information, a copy of their registration and more. That information can help the government and state quickly assess each person suspected of illegally registering to vote, said the letter sent to San Bernardino County voting officials. The letter says the government's list of suspected noncitizen voters includes 1,133 people from the inland Southern California county. California’s secretary of state and the Los Angeles County registrar have opposed the federal government’s demands. In legal filings, lawyers for California say the request threatens to delay the certification of the vote and undermine the legitimacy of the November midterms. They have also argued that the federal government's data is unreliable and that their demands risk disenfranchisement of citizens. Voting is underway in California, with the state's more than 23 million registered voters receiving ballots in the mail earlier this month. The state said in legal filings that over 330,000 mail-in ballots have already been counted. The letters on Friday came on the heels of statewide sweep by federal authorities earlier in the week, where 28 people from the list of 20,000 were charged with illegally registering to vote. Some were also charged with illegally voting and lying on naturalization paperwork. Those charges could lead to years in prison. articles.title: Judge rules Jane Doe in Cornell case can remain anonymous while pursuing lawsuit
articles.summary: A judge in New York on Friday decided the former Cornell University student known as Jane Doe can pursue her sexual assault claim against the university and seven fraternity members while remaining anonymous. Permission to proceed in litigation under a pseudonym is not automatic, but the judge said "the notoriety of the allegations and widespread reports of certain malicious actors' behavior" warranted anonymity. Jane Doe says she felt 'unsupported and disbelieved' by Cornell president The judge's decision came with a warning to those who have threatened Jane Doe and others connected to the case. "While the Court is cognizant that some members of the public have made it their mission to try and identify Jane Doe, and have likewise tried to use what they believe to be Jane Doe's identity to harass and threaten certain individuals allegedly tied to her, the Court issues the following words of caution: cyberstalking and engaging in or encouraging threats across state lines, whether it be of Jane Doe, any of the named defendants, or their attorneys, can be considered a federal crime and perpetrators of those acts may be subjecting themselves to prosecution," Judge Phaedra Perry-Bond wrote in her opinion. Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images - PHOTO: A hand written sign is seen before a rally in support of a former Cornell University student known as Jane Doe at the Ithaca Commons, October 13, 2026 in Ithaca, New York. Former Cornell fraternity president dropped from Jane Doe lawsuit Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit alleging she had been drugged and gang-raped at the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024. All seven men named in the lawsuit have denied wrongdoing and no criminal charges have been filed in the case. Her attorney, Thomas Giuffra, has previously told ABC News that Jane Doe and her family have been subjected to threats, doxxing and other forms of harassment. New York Attorney General Letitia James, who was appointed by Gov. Kathy Hochul, is conducting an investigation into the incident. Cornell, which said it fully supports the appointment of a special prosecutor, is also conducting an internal probe of its response to the allegations. The case has rocked the university and started conversations about treatment of sexual assault allegations on college campuses across the country. Cornell has said it takes allegations of allegations of sexual violence "extremely seriously" and that it "investigated and adjudicated the allegations consistent with university policies." At the same time, the university has said it is committed to taking additional steps to improve campus safety. articles.title: Ukraine says Starlink restrictions remain despite Trump's claims they're lifted
articles.summary: Watch: Who controls Ukraine's access to Starlink? Ukraine is still recording issues with the Starlink internet network, sources within the defence ministry say, after Donald Trump said limits had been reversed by Elon Musk who owns the satellite system. The sources told the BBC that instances of drones experiencing connection loss at speeds of 161km/h (100mph) were being recorded, hampering military operations. The US president had denied instructing the tech billionaire to restrict connectivity to Starlink's military-grade counterpart, Starshield, before saying on Thursday that Musk had "put it back". Asked on Friday, Trump said: "If there is a problem, I will get it straightened out." Trump added: "I have not spoken to him. I might have to, but I have not. I've heard it was fixed, but if it's not, I'll speak to him." Musk previously said he was not behind the slowdown, which affected Ukraine's ability to use attack drones and co-ordinate defensive operations. Trump told reporters he did not think the tech billionaire had too much power. The Ukrainian defence ministry sources said the military was constantly monitoring the performance of both the Starlink and Starshield networks. They added that there was "currently no confirmation that these restrictions have been lifted". Last week, Kyiv said uplink speeds to the low Earth orbit satellites had been restricted, affecting the speed at which drones could travel. Any drone travelling faster than 100mph lost its connection, officials said. Shortly after, Musk said that Starshield , which Ukraine uses for some of its operation, was controlled by the US military and suggested that the Pentagon could be behind the issues. The White House has since repeatedly denied deliberately placing limits on the network in Ukraine. In a call with Trump on Friday evening, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham "underlined the importance for Ukraine to have full access to Starlink so they can continue to defend themselves against Russia's full-scale invasion", Downing Street said in a statement. Why is Starlink internet so important on the battlefield in Ukraine? Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, depending on what communications are needed. The networks use 10,000 satellites to provide connectivity, particularly in remote areas and on the battlefield. Starshield allows Ukrainian drone operators to see targets in real time, as well as operate interceptor drones. Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work. One Ukrainian soldier said there was "simply no alternative" to Starshield, adding that earlier in the week, connectivity had been cutting out when his unit had been travelling in a car at 80km/h (50 mph). "I'll tell you this much: God forbid they shut it off completely - it would be an absolute catastrophe," he told the BBC. "We need a backup option for securing communications and internet." Another soldier said they had reverted to the "proven algorithms" they used before they had Starlink when it initially started playing up, but stressed that Ukrainian forces did need the network, citing its speed. "Even one or two seconds is critical when we can transfer data and orders faster," she said. "You can really feel that advantage on the battlefield." Ukrainian reports of a slowdown to the service came during a tense diplomatic row between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky about Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies. [BBC] Trump said the strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are crucial to stemming the main revenue source for Moscow's war effort, have pushed global prices higher. While the attacks have had an impact on global fuel prices, rises seen this year have primarily been due to the Iran war . Zelensky said the US had also threatened to withdraw intelligence sharing if the strikes did not stop, something Trump later denied. The row prompted a war of words between the two world leaders, with Trump suggesting it was time for Ukraine to get a new president and Zelensky implying Trump was not a real leader. Earlier on Thursday - before Trump's comments - Zelensky had said the speed of the system had still not been restored fully. "I am waiting to hear from US Secretary of State [Marco] Rubio. He promised to get back to me with information within 48 hours or so." The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump had told Musk that he was frustrated the Starlink system's speeds were still capped, and that the system was working closer to normal following that conversation. articles.title: Employee error blamed for toxic chemical leak that sent 60 people to hospital in Ohio
articles.summary: A chemical leak that sent 60 people to the hospital and forced hundreds of people to flee their homes has been blamed on an employee error. Mayor Wade Kapszukiewicz announced the cause of the tank leak at a news conference on Friday and said that all remaining evacuation orders in Toledo , Ohio . The chemical leak happened Tuesday night when an employee of MC Tank Transport “introduced a temperature level to the tank in the process of trying to transfer the liquid" that caused a chemical reaction, the mayor said. MC Tank Transport said the tank contained glycidyl methacrylate , which it described as “an industrial chemical used to make certain plastics, paints and coatings perform better.” A plume of smokes rises from MC Tank Transport Inc., where a chemical tank exploded overnight, prompting hundreds of residents to evacuate or shelter in place amid concerns about a potential toxic release, Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026 (AP) The evacuation orders were lifted after the company finished venting the tank that ruptured. That allowed a hazmat team to enter the site and test safety levels. “At this time, we do feel confident that the site is safe," Toledo Fire and Rescue Battalion Chief Blake Molnar said. Dr Brian Kaminski, vice president of medical affairs for ProMedica hospitals, said about 60 patients were treated at the hospital, most suffering relatively minor symptoms. A small number of patients who had underlying health conditions were admitted, he said, and all patients were expected to recover. The company has “accepted responsibility” for what happened, the mayor said. The U.S. EPA on the scene near MC Tank Transport Inc. (AP) “There was no fire, there was no explosion. There was a very serious chemical reaction, which now happily has run its course, and we’re now finally able to return to some level of normalcy here in our community," he said. Based on data that officials have seen so far, the amount of the chemical in the air didn't reach levels high enough to have “a long-term meaningful impact on human health,” according to Kapszukiewicz. articles.title: Wells Fargo says customers may be liable for unwanted purchases by their AI agents
articles.summary: Citi Bank, Wells Fargo, Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase have taken steps to limit third-party AI agents from accessing their platforms and services, and others are following suit. The banks’ decisions, first reported by Axios , come amid mounting concern over AI agents taking unwanted actions on behalf of users. Two-thirds of chief information security officers surveyed in financial services and software ranked agentic AI among their top three cybersecurity risks, and more than one-third named it as their top concern, according to a 2026 study by Palo Alto Networks . “We do not permit third-party AI agents or assistants to log into a customer's account or transact directly within our digital banking platforms,” a Citi spokesperson wrote to USA TODAY. Citi customers can authorize agents to “limited, read-only access to their account information with certain Citi-approved open banking providers,” the statement continued. Citi has not seen reports of agents accessing client accounts. “There’s a window of vulnerability where the systems, the banks, the users are all vulnerable to the speed with which AI is being weaponized,” said Andre Durand, founder and CEO of Ping Identity, which sells identity security infrastructure to financial institutions. He cited concern over AI being used to perpetrate fraud and scams at higher levels as well as fear that agents could be compromised or decide to take malicious action on their own. In an October report by Ping , 71% of consumers surveyed reported concern that an AI agent acting on their behalf could misrepresent their personality or values. However, less than a quarter said they refuse to trust AI with any financial transaction, at 22%. Durand said that “the challenge that we're having right now is how can we detect that it is an agent and not a human asking. And if we can detect that it’s an agent not a human, how do we know that the agent is acting on the authority of the human?” Agent restrictions Bank of America, Capital One and four other global banks created a coalition in September to warn that agentic technology is moving faster than industry standards and protections are keeping up. The coalition highlighted the risk that AI shopping agents pose in particular. “When you give the agent your credentials, it is you authorizing the payment. So we’re just trying to work with these companies and with the industry to say, put a human being in the loop,” Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan told Bloomberg on Oct. 15. “So before you pay, you authorize it, so that we know that you know you’re paying for something.” According to Moynihan, Bank of America is restricting AI agents’ access to consumer deposits and is working with companies to develop protocols on agents. JPMorgan Chase CEO confirmed to Bloomberg last week that JPMorgan Chase is also blocking outside agents from accessing customer-account information. Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase did not immediately respond to a request for comment from USA TODAY. Wells Fargo has also “taken steps to block unauthorized agents from accessing customer accounts,” a bank spokesperson told USA TODAY. According to Wells Fargo’s updated online access agreement , authorized representative or delegate transactions – including transactions of agents – are considered authorized, unless the user explicitly tells the bank they are not authorized and the bank “have had reasonable opportunity to act on your notification.” The agreement is set to take effect on Nov. 24. It includes a section on third-party AI agents in which users agree that they are "solely responsible” for supervising agents, that the bank may act on the instructions of agents and that all transactions taken by authorized representatives such as agents – “including those you did not want or intend” – are considered authorized. “If you permit an AI Agent or other third party access to the Service, you acknowledge that doing so may adversely impact the commercially reasonable security procedures that you've otherwise agreed to, and you accept the risk of such access,” according to the agreement. Durand said he wasn’t aware of specific instances of agents hacking into banks, but added, “I don’t think a lot of stuff is being reported” in regards to agents or AI activity at banks. Alternative options In addition to blocking unauthorized agents from logging in on behalf of clients, Charles Schwab created its own AI assistant , called Charley, which cannot execute trades but can answer questions and complete routine tasks. Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said in an interview with Bloomberg on Oct. 16 that the bank is blocking between “tens and twenties” of attempts by major AI agents to access and manipulate client funds. As AI agent usage grows — Meta reported that Muse grew to 10 million users on Oct. 21 — Durand emphasized the need for better authentication systems. One-time passwords sent to emails are no longer secure enough, he said, because agents often have access to email. “Passkeys and biometrics ensure that the human is the one authenticating, and/or that the human is the one authorizing,” Durand said. Greta Reich covers the artificial intelligence industry for USA TODAY through a fellowship from the Tarbell Center for AI Journalism. Funders do not provide editorial input. articles.title: Oil prices hit 6-month high over fears of escalating fighting in the Middle East
articles.summary: Oil prices climbed to a 6-month high on Friday as traders priced the odds of escalating fighting in the Middle East.  Attacks near the Red Sea also stoked worries of further constraints on oil supplies from the region. Brent crude ( BZ=F )  futures for December delivery settled at $116.72 per barrel. The international benchmark posted its third consecutive week of gains. Meanwhile, West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) closed just above $103 a barrel. President Trump telegraphed an escalation in Iran after the midterm elections and an extended stand-off, with the Strait of Hormuz remaining at the center of the conflict. This week, the New York Times reported that the US and Israel have reportedly drawn up plans for renewed attacks on Iran after the Nov. 3 elections. The US has ordered nonessential embassy personnel to depart Saudi Arabia after a series of attacks at the country's airports and oil fields . President Trump has said he will not attack Iran before the midterms and has suggested that fuel prices will fall afterward. Meanwhile, the Red Sea area has seen increased attacks recently, including on Saudi Arabian airports and on an Aramco oil field this week. Saudi Aramco on Thursday ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran , marking the oil giant's first such evacuation since the Iran war began. On Friday, the national price of gasoline stood at $4.29 per gallon, roughly $1.22 higher than a year ago. Diesel hovered around $6.31, about $2.68 more than this time last year. A power outage at a refinery in the Chicago area is expected to send refined fuel prices even higher in the region. "You're going to see a lot of $5 gas prices in places like Michigan, Ohio, Minnesota, Illinois, and Indiana," Gulf Oil chief energy adviser Tom Kloza told Yahoo Finance on Thursday. Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance. articles.title: Democrats are favored to flip the House, but Republicans still have a path to victory
articles.summary: It's crunch time. With less than two weeks to go until the 2026 midterm elections, Democratic and Republican candidates for the U.S. House of Representatives nationwide are making one last push to persuade voters in their districts — and help their party win or retain control of the chamber on Nov. 3. The stakes are high. President Trump has enjoyed complete Republican control of Congress for the first half of his second term. Flipping the House would give Democrats the power to block parts of the president's agenda, investigate his administration and even impeach him (again) . Historically speaking, a president's party almost always loses seats when voters return to the polls to judge his first two years in office. (The average number lost since World War II? Twenty-six .) Sometimes, the backlash is so pervasive that the president's party loses seats across a wide range of competitive districts — a phenomenon known as a "wave" election. But the past doesn't necessarily predict the future, and Republicans have certain advantages today that they didn't have before. Here's what needs to happen for each party to come out on top. Yahoo The races to watch The first thing to know about any House election is that while all 435 congressional districts are technically up for grabs, roughly 80% of those contests (representing about 350 seats) are not considered competitive. House incumbents have always had huge advantages: money and name recognition, mostly. But their head start has only widened in recent years as partisan polarization and redistricting have helped make the vast majority of congressional districts "safe" for one party . These days, incumbents tend to focus more on fending off primary challengers. The general election can be a breeze in comparison. As a result, this year's true battleground is relatively small. According to the nonpartisan Cook Political Report's " race ratings ," just 17 contests are genuine "tossups" at this point. Another 16 "lean Democratic," and 17 "lean Republican." There's also a third competitive category that includes 18 seats where Democrats are the "likely" winners, and 13 seats where the same could be said about Republicans. That's 81 competitive districts — again, out of 435. It's clear from looking at this year's ratings which party is playing more defense and which is playing more offense — and where. Only 30 Democratic seats are considered competitive, and more than half of them (17) are "likely" to remain Democratic, according to Cook. Just five Democratic seats are tossups. Just two are leaning Republican. In contrast, a full 51 Republican seats are considered competitive — and about half of them are tossups (12) or leaning Democratic (12). Geographically, this year's tossups are concentrated in certain kinds of places: Rust Belt districts in states that have swung from party to party in the past (such as Michigan, Pennsylvania and Ohio); Mid-Atlantic suburbs (in states such as New York, Virginia and North Carolina) where Trump has scrambled some of the usual coalitions; and Sun Belt districts (think Florida, Texas, California and Nevada) where Latinos factor heavily. Trump carried many of these areas in 2024 . On Friday, Cook shifted another 19 of its race ratings toward Democrats — part of a pattern that has seen the outlet move a total of 63 race ratings toward Democrats over the last month. "Republicans' path to keeping control of the House has all but evaporated," Cook's House analyst wrote . "Following this latest round of ratings changes, Democrats now are favored outright in the 218 seats they need to win control of the House. In other words, 220 seats are rated either Solid, Likely or Lean Democrat. Republicans, meanwhile, are favored in 198 seats, rated Solid, Likely, or Lean Republican." Overall, the map gives Democrats more pickup options — which means more paths to a House majority. The path to a Democratic House Senate and governor contests can be quirky — more state-specific and personality-driven. But national dynamics tend to play a larger role in shaping the composition of the incoming House. So it's not just a matter of who has more targets on the board. It's that the board itself tends to tilt to one side or the other, taking most of those targets with it. A recent example was the 2010 midterm election, when impatience with America's slow recovery from the 2008 financial collapse and frustration with President Barack Obama's response helped Republicans gain 64 House seats. Beyond the history of midterm backlash against the president's party, Democrats have two big advantages right now. One is that the current Republican majority is so minuscule — just 219 votes to 214, including an independent who caucuses with Republicans — that Democrats only need a net gain of three seats to win back the House. The other is that the board seems to be tilting in Democrats' favor — assuming the polls are right. Surveys suggest there's one underlying factor pulling the national electorate to the left: dissatisfaction with Trump. According to the data journalists at Silver Bulletin , an average of 60% of Americans currently disapprove of how Trump is handling his job vs. 37% who approve. That puts the president's net approval rating at -23% — near his all-time low. Trump is earning even lower marks on voters' top issue this year: the cost of living . Shortly after he returned to office, roughly equal numbers of Americans approved and disapproved of how the president was handling inflation. But today — as tariffs and the Iran war help drive prices up — 71% disapprove and 25% approve . That's a 46-point gap. President Trump arrives to speak at a campaign rally at F&M Bank Arena on Oct. 10, 2026, in Clarksville, Tenn. AP Photo/Alex Brandon Democrats aren't particularly popular. But for the party in power, it may be hard to overcome this level of dissatisfaction with the status quo. That's why, when pollsters ask their so-called generic ballot question — If an election for U.S. Congress were held today, which party's candidate would you vote for in your district? — Americans are currently giving Democrats a substantial lead of more than 9 percentage points , on average. Making matters worse for Republicans, that lead has grown over the last month as swing voters who favored Trump in 2024 — including some Latinos and independents — say they're planning to vote Democratic. To put a 9-point lead in perspective, Democrats were leading by an average of 7.6 points on the generic ballot at this point in 2018, with Trump as president and Republican majorities in the House and Senate. On Election Day, they picked up 41 seats and flipped the House. If the polls are right, Democrats might win control of the House again. The path to a Republican House But are the polls right? Recently, Republicans have pointed to some surprising survey results on the Senate side — including Democratic leads in rural red states such as Iowa , Kansas and Nebraska — to argue that pollsters might be misjudging public sentiment. They're not wrong to say the polls have missed in the past. Polling errors are commonplace; they happen in most elections. But they tend to be random and to change directions from one cycle to another . The Trump era has been a little different. In each of the three presidential contests that Trump himself has competed in, the final average of polls conducted before Election Day underestimated Republicans' performance in the popular vote by an average of 3.8 percentage points, according to data journalist Nate Silver . The theory is that a phenomenon called nonresponse bias — in which Democratic voters are more eager or available to respond to pollsters than Republican voters — might have made Democratic support look stronger than it actually was. Pollsters try to adjust for this by weighting their results — that is, using statistical methods to give less weight to respondents who are overrepresented demographically and more weight to respondents who are underrepresented demographically. But it's difficult to predict in advance who will show up on Election Day. This time around, there are signs that rural Republicans are not responding to pollsters in certain states . Could that mean Republican candidates in those places will outperform their polling? Possibly. But experts say it may also mean that rural Republicans are less supportive of the GOP than they were in 2024 — potentially voting Democratic or staying home on Nov. 3. A voter walks toward his polling place. REUTERS / REUTERS After all, there's been virtually no polling bias toward Democrats in Trump era elections when Trump himself wasn't on the ballot. In fact, the polls since 2016 have overestimated Republican support in midterm elections (by an average of 0.2%) and off-year, special and runoff elections (by an average of 1.3%), according to Silver . Either way, pollsters aren't seeing signs of this rural effect in most states — and even if they were, it might make only a minor dent in Democrats' 9-point national lead . Redistricting is the other Republican advantage. House redistricting efforts typically take place every 10 years, after each new census reveals changes in population distribution. But last summer, Trump successfully pushed GOP legislators in Texas to pass new congressional district boundaries five years earlier than normal to help Republicans win five additional House seats in 2026. This kicked off a tit-for-tat cycle that saw nine states adopt new congressional maps for the midterms — some to benefit Democrats, others Republicans. Now that the dust has settled, Cook projects that Republicans could win nine seats because of redistricting (in Alabama, Florida, Louisiana, North Carolina, Ohio, Tennessee and Texas), while Democrats could win five (in California and Utah). If that plays out, it would net the GOP four seats overall. It's not what Republicans initially hoped to gain from gerrymandering. "We're not gonna win all 13 of those redistricted seats. That's correct. We're not," GOP House Majority Whip Tom Emmer of Minnesota told Axios recently . But it's also not nothing. The hope for the GOP is that some combination of polling error and redistricting boost — along with a late influx of hundreds of millions of dollars to help defend districts Trump won in 2024 — will be just enough to preserve their slim House majority. articles.title: 2 former FBI officials charged with lying to Congress about Hunter Biden laptop probe
articles.summary: Jeanine Pirro, U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia.  (Aaron Schwartz / Bloomberg via Getty ) WASHINGTON — Two former FBI officials who have come under withering criticism from allies of President Donald Trump have been charged with allegedly lying to Congress over the investigation into former President Joe Biden’s son Hunter Biden . A court docket shows that Nikki Floris, the former deputy assistant director of the FBI’s Counterintelligence Division, and Bradley Benavides, another FBI official, were facing one count of the rarely-charged criminal offense which can be difficult to prosecute. Hunter Biden was investigated, charged and eventually convicted of  gun and tax crimes, before his father pardoned him shortly leaving office. U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro said in a social media post that Floris and Benavides had surrendered Friday morning. She alleged that the duo lied about their roles in the Foreign Influence Task Force and “about their roles in the FBI’s Hunter Biden investigations.” Attorneys for Floris said in a statement that Floris was “a patriot” who “served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years” and was charged so the administration could “push a false narrative for a shot at political points.” Deputy Assistant Director for Counterterrorism at the FBI Nikki Floris testifies before the House Judiciary Committee hearing on Capitol Hill on Oct. 22, 2019. (Susan Walsh / AP) Attorneys Margaret Donovan, Chris Mattei, Mary Dohrmann and Kyle R. Freeny said in a statement that the “DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts. It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election.” One of the attorneys for Benavides, Ronald S. Safer, called the charges a disgrace and said Friday that his client “worked tirelessly to protect the public from terrorists and agents of foreign governments” for 20 years and “protected our democracy against those who would destroy it.” “In return, today, the government that he loves brought baseless criminal charges against him in a transparently political complaint,” Safer said. “This is another sad day for the Department of Justice. But now we are in court, and the truth will come out: Brad Benavides is a true patriot who devoted his career to protecting this country and its people.” Trump commented on the case Friday evening while speaking to reporters in Florida. “I don’t know exactly what it is, but I heard they were arrested or charged. And I heard they were bad people,” Trump said. “You know, they’re crooked people. You know what they are? Dirty cops, like Comey.” The Trump administration is pursuing a separate case against former FBI Director James Comey, a frequent target of Trump’s, over a photo he posted on Instagram, and later deleted, of seashells arranged to spell out “8647” that prosecutors said amounted to a threat against the president. Comey has not yet entered a plea in the case but has said it did not occur to him that the numbers could be interpreted in a violent way . Asked on Friday evening if he believes the FBI was protecting the Bidens before the 2020 election, Trump said, “Yeah, I guess.” The case against the two former FBI officials was brought through a criminal complaint. Neither defendant has yet been indicted by a federal grand jury in D.C., where grand jurors have been skeptical of cases brought during Trump’s second term. Earlier this year, federal grand jurors rejected an attempt to indict six sitting Democratic members of Congress over a video Trump criticized. Flores was the FBI’s security lead for the 2020 presidential election, which Trump has falsely claimed was stolen. A mob of Trump supporters violently broke into the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021, in a failed effort to stop the certification of Democrat Joe Biden as president. They beat and bloodied law enforcement, shattered windows and broke through barriers. She joined the FBI as an intelligence analyst in 2005, working on the director’s daily briefing staff and helped produce intelligence documents. She was promoted in 2017 to the department’s counterterrorism division. Benavides is a former colleague of Floris who focused on election security, foreign influence and Chinese intelligence threats. Floris has also been under criticism from Republicans over emails in which she discussed intelligence work that were obtained by Congress and declassified in July by Trump. Republicans have alleged that FBI officials buried what they describe as a credible report on China’s efforts to influence the election in an effort to protect then-FBI Director Christopher Wray. Intelligence officials and her legal team have said the pullback was a standard administrative move for a report that may have been unverified or had flawed intelligence. articles.title: 中国铜进口溢价创12年新高：减产风险会否再推铜价上行？
articles.summary: 10月23日，国内铜进口溢价持续攀升，洋山铜溢价升至168美元/吨，创2014年以来新高。与此同时，国内铜库存处于相对低位，上海期货交易所铜库存约7.4万吨，仅为美国COMEX铜库存的1/10。作为全球最大的铜需求国，中国铜进口溢价的快速上行表明当前铜现货供应显著偏紧。 在供给端，另一项重要变化在于国内铜冶炼厂减产风险上升。受铜精矿供应紧张、现货加工费（TC/RC）跌入负值区间以及副产品硫酸等价格自高位回落影响，部分冶炼企业已开始通过检修、降低开工率以及减少精矿加工量来控制亏损，部分头部企业的粗炼产能受影响比例或达30%；预计今明两年中国精炼铜产量将面临显著的减产压力。 在SHFE库存偏低、进口溢价快速走高的背景下，矿端或冶炼端的边际扰动更容易被放大并传导至现货价格。国内现货铜溢价于9月底升至1375元/吨的阶段性高位，尽管随后有所回落，但近期仍反弹至850元/吨。 在现货铜价高企、进口溢价高涨及减产预期下，7、8两月精炼铜进口量快速收缩；尽管9月份大幅回升，但同比仍大幅回落17%。受检修和减产影响，预计Q4精炼铜产量较此前预测减少29.3万吨，全年产量仅增1%至1370万吨，明显低于去年同期近15%的增速。 海外矿端约束同样强化。全球最大的铜矿生产国智利正遭受极端天气（如超级厄尔尼诺带来的强降雨）、老旧矿山品位衰退、致命事故及劳工纠纷的多重打击，其产量降至近20年来的最低水平。8月份，智利铜产量36.6万吨，环比降8.5%，同比降13%；1-8月累计降8%。全球铜产业链在冶炼端与矿山端同时面临供给挤压。 非美可流通铜稀缺，铜价上行凸性增强

articles.title: “共识交易”的瓦解和新共识的诞生！高盛解答：为何机构当下都在大幅减仓AI
articles.summary: 此前市场极度拥挤的“做多AI，做空其他一切”交易正在经历痛苦的解构，创纪录抛售下，超大规模云厂商迎“变现大考”。 10月22日，高盛欧洲固定收益与股票（FICC & Equities）交易主管Rich Privorotsky在位于伦敦的高盛交易室接受了播客栏目《The Markets》的访谈。Privorotsky透露了一个极具冲击力的数据： “上周我们的主经纪商业务账簿（Prime book）上，出现了有史以来最大规模的科技股抛售。” 面对这波抛售潮，正在进行中的三季度财报季显得尤为关键。市场的焦点已从单纯的“讲故事”转向了严苛的业绩兑现。Privorotsky指出，市场预计明年AI的资本支出（Capex）将高达1.1万亿美元，但这已不足以让投资者买单。 “仅仅说你花了很多钱是不够的，你还需要证明未完成的订单正在转化为实质性的收入。”Privorotsky强调，“他们必须在推动资本支出的同时展示这些支出的回报。这不是一个轻松的局面。”他表示，云业务的增长、变现能力以及自由现金流实现收支平衡的速度，将对目前极其敏感的信用市场产生重大影响。 基础设施与资金双重掣肘：明年存在“40-50吉瓦”电力缺口 在AI狂热降温的背后，是现实世界中基础设施和资金池的硬性约束。市场目前正在与三个核心问题作斗争，首当其冲的便是资金成本的溢出效应和电力供应。 Privorotsky指出，杠杆率较高的AI交易领域（如新兴的云服务提供商）正面临严峻的融资考验：“这些企业在寻找融资来兑现AI支出时是否会遇到困难？” 更现实的物理瓶颈在于电力交付能力。 他提出了一组关键数据：“明年的电力缺口大约在40到50吉瓦。如果你无法获得实际为数据中心供电的能源，你还能消耗掉你已经提前订购的芯片吗？”这些担忧导致投资者进入“去风险模式”，通过做空AI和AI资本支出交易来降低增长预期，同时资金涌入债券市场避险。 宏观范式重塑：从“储蓄过剩”走向“支出过剩” 站在宏观周期的角度，Privorotsky描绘了一幅深刻的范式转换图景。 他表示，自己的整个职业生涯都处于“储蓄过剩”的环境中——系统里的钱多到不知道该怎么办。但现在，情况发生了“地震般的剧变（Seismic shift）”。 “在过去的一年里，我们预计将在AI资本支出上花费超过1万亿美元，而全球大多数政府都在运行财政赤字。 我们正处于一个‘支出过剩’的时代。” 这种转变推高了资本成本，并自然而然地挤出了处于边缘、资质较差的借款人。 他观察到，这种压力不仅体现在CCC级信用利差的大幅走阔上，甚至蔓延到了主权债务领域（如面临高额财政赤字的法国国债）。再加上居高不下的能源价格，整体市场的风险偏好正在被显著削弱。 市场情绪走向两极，“成也AI，败也AI” 在复杂的宏观和微观交织下，投资者的焦虑情绪出现了奇特的“极化”现象。 Privorotsky分享了他本周与投资者交流的见闻：“我遇到一些投资者说，‘我担心无法交付算力，这让我害怕’；然后我又遇到了另一批投资者，他们说，‘我担心我们会过度交付算力，这让我害怕’。不知何故，两个完全互斥的结果构成了市场担忧的总和。” 由于能源价格对经济产生重大影响（标普500虽然表现平稳，但中位数股票实际上已下跌超过10%），金融状况指数（FCI）大幅收紧，迫使美联储采取更多行动。 Privorotsky曾坚信“原油决定一切（As goes oil, so goes everything else）”，但他现在承认， 在当前的市场语境下，逻辑已经演变为“AI决定一切（As goes AI, so goes everything else）”。 尽管短期内面临压力，但Privorotsky并未完全悲观。他认为现货市场的算力价格每天都在创出新高，需求依然“贪婪且永无止境”。在交易策略上，他表示虽然目前信念度不高，但已遭遇大幅降级的“电气化”相关资产、民用航空航天资产以及部分运输板块，目前已经具备了可观的安全边际，值得保持谨慎乐观。 以下为播客对话全文翻译： Chris Hussey 00:00 这里是《 The Markets 》。我是 Chris Hussey ，今天是 10 月的星期四。我从伦敦高盛交易大厅请到了 Rich Probarowski ，他是 Prevo 旗下 FIC 与股票业务的欧洲股票交易主管。非常感谢你来做客。谢谢你们的邀请。 Hussey ，我们就直接进入正题吧，因为，你知道的，你写的东西我全都读了，而且你提出过一个很好的观点——今年夏初的时候，那个痛苦交易，也就是大家不得不去追的那个交易，是做多 AI 、做空其他一切。它已经有点变成了、很大的一笔交易。现在随着我们进入三季报季，这个交易似乎正在瓦解。到底发生了什么？你认为接下来会怎么演变？股票市场出现了极其严重的集中度，而且我得说，过去几周对这类一致性交易来说尤其痛苦。 Rich Privorotsky 00:48 大家的仓位高度集中在 AI 、半导体和超大规模云厂商上。我想说，眼下市场大概正应对三个不同的问题。其一，显然，我们在资本成本方面出现了溢出效应。我认为这几乎随处可见，无论是 CCC 级利差、欧洲的主权利差，还是 AI 交易中那些杠杆更高的、最为尖端的部分——其中 Neo 云（ Neo clouds ）尤其突出。所以，这就变成了一个供给问题。你知道，这些企业会不会难以找到融资来交付所有这些 AI 支出？第二点同样关于供给：我们是否真的有能力通电并交付吉瓦级电力，市场对此存在疑问，明年的区间大概是 20 到 40 、 50 吉瓦。所以，如果你拿不到电力真正让数据中心通电，你真的能够、能够消化掉你已经提前下单的那些芯片吗，所以。 Rich Privorotsky 01:38 这些都是萦绕在市场上空的担忧，而这一切叠加之后，已经把大家推进了一种去风险的心态；这种心态的具体表现，是通过 AI 交易和 AI 资本开支交易压低了增长预期。而在另一面，随着增长预期下修，债券一直在上涨——这一点完全不在任何人的剧本里。 Rich Privorotsky 01:56 好的，这里信息量很大。不过我们把焦点放在不远的未来、其实也就是当下 ——三季报季。我们已经身处其中了，一些大型科技股已经公布业绩，但后面还有很多。三季报季里你最密切关注的是什么？是的，我认为我们即将进入超大规模云厂商财报的核心部分，我觉得真正重要的不仅是看到资本开支维持在高位——市场普遍预期明年在 1.1 万亿美元——而最重要的是，要看到，你知道的，云业务的持续增长和变现。所以，光说自己在花很多钱是不够的，你还需要证明积压订单正在有意义地转化成收入。所以我认为这对市场会非常关键。我认为，他们实现自由现金流打平的这个过渡会有多快——相对于市场预期。可能会对信贷市场产生重大影响，而信贷市场已经变得极其敏感。所以对我而言，真的，有很多东西可以看。我会说，来自经济其他领域的。但我认为市场的焦点会真正落在超大规模云厂商身上，然后是交付的质量，而不仅仅是支出。对这些公司来说，要翻过这道坎太难了。他们必须一边继续推高资本开支，一边还得向你展示这些资本开支的回报。这不是一个轻松的局面，不是吗？是的，不是。但你看，我的意思是，当前的大背景是这样的：你看到算力价格在现货市场上每天都在创下新高。对他们所卖的东西，需求是永不满足的，所以我想说。 Chris Hussey 03:23 用稍微乐观一点的眼光看，他们应该有一个相当不错的故事可讲。好的，里奇，说起来确实有一阵子没请你上节目了。你上次来还是在一月。但这一年里，你一直是秉持那句口诀的人之一 ——石油怎么走，其他一切都怎么走。这还是那句口诀吗？是的，我认为我们在能源方面遇到了极其棘手的大环境。而且，你知道，我认为。 Rich Privorotsky 03:46 市场、股票市场，我认为，已经尽其所能地去忽视、并把能源价格的上涨隔离在一个角落里。但这其实不太公平，因为标普指数在隔离这件事上做得很好，可是中位数个股实际上已经下跌远超 10% 。所以这对利率产生了影响。它也影响了 FCI 。事实上我们经历了一次大规模的 FCI 收紧，这在某种意义上也倒逼美联储做了更多。而且我们重新定价了整整一轮加息周期。所以我认为能源在这中间占了很大一部分。我认为我们仍然因为能源而负担着大量的风险溢价。显然，接下来几周这些事情会如何演进，对整个风险资产而言将非常关键。而我乐观的看法是，我们会在未来几周内获得某种形式的解决。但我必须承认，我之前以为这在两个月前就该发生了，在这一点上我判断得有点偏了。我想我们都是。当然，你说的 FCI ，指的是金融状况指数，它是。 Chris Hussey 04:35 算是衡量经济、或者说衡量所有经济脉冲是收紧还是放松的一个尺度。它不只是关于利率。当你看一个 FCI 时，有时它可能是石油，有时它也可能是股票。好的，这个观点不错。关于石油这块。 Chris Hussey 04:48 不过，与那笔石油交易相关的，还有你在年初时说的一句话，那就是：我想做多名义资产 ——在一个 GDP 增长强劲、而且看起来依然非常强劲的扩张世界里，而且通胀很高，我就是想做多这类东西，也就是大量的大宗商品。今天你怎么看这笔名义资产的交易？它现在还是值得配置的地方吗？ Rich Privorotsky 05:11 我认为，要回答这个问题，我得先回答那个价值万亿美元的问题，也就是： AI 支出接下来会如何，以及相对市场预期而言，它的可持续性如何？ Rich Privorotsky 05:19 因为现实是，当我们在重新定价它的时候，我们重新定价了一切，包括大宗商品，包括名义资产。我的直觉是，我们有点把孩子连同洗澡水一起倒掉了，而且我们显然已经开始担忧它的每一个维度。说得具体一点：这周我见到一些投资者，他们说「我担心算力交付不出来，这让我害怕」。然后我又见到另外一批投资者，他们说「我担心我们会过度交付算力，这让我害怕」。不知怎么的，我们得到了两个互斥的结果，而它们同时又构成了市场担忧的总和。 Rich Privorotsky 05:50 所以我认为，从大格局上看名义资产仍是你想要待的地方，除非我们陷入、一场反通胀式的崩坏，也就是资本开支放缓、所有人都不得不收缩、迎来一轮真正的信贷周期。换作三个月前我会说，这种风险很低，而现在无疑高得多了。但我的直觉是，从中长期看，那仍然是你想待的地方。不过我认为，现在在组合里多加一点杠铃策略或许更明智些。听起来你的意思是，以前也许是石油怎么走、其他一切就怎么走，现在是 —— AI 怎么走。 Chris Hussey 06:22 其他一切就怎么走。是这样吗？我认为，冒着过度简化的风险说，这大概是对的。是的，里奇，谢谢你愿意过度简化。我自己就是「过度简化先生」，所以我很高兴你能走到这一步。当然，这里面有一部分会是一轮大的信贷周期，而三个月前你并不担心信贷周期，现在你担心的程度多了一些。跟我们聊聊这个。你看到信贷出现裂缝了吗？你指的是欧洲主权债正在发生的问题，还是更多指的是我们在企业端看到的那些信用问题？ Rich Privorotsky 06:51 我整个职业生涯，可以说都身处在一个 ——储蓄过剩之中。你知道，系统里的钱多到我们不知道该怎么用。而就在过去这一年，我们的预计是要在 AI 资本开支上花掉超过 1 万亿美元。 Rich Privorotsky 07:05 全球大多数政府都在跑财政赤字。我们现在处在一个支出过剩之中。从事物运作的方式、以及资本成本会变成什么样来看，这是一次非常巨大的结构性转变。所以，我认为这自然会把那些处在边缘、资质不是最优的借款人挤出去。我认为你已经能从 CCC 级利差上看到这一点——公允地说，考虑到那边所发生事件的构成，这多少有些特殊性。但它们确实变动很大，而且已经稍微溢出到了信用市场更广泛的部分。然后显然，你还会有法国主权债的担忧，也就是：作为一个在这种环境下背负着巨额财政赤字的主权国家，它们同样都会被挤出去。所以我认为所有这些都在产生影响，同时我们再回到石油交易上——只要能源价格维持高位，它就会压低风险偏好。而且，我认为对这类资产来说，现在有点像是一个买方市场。是的，从储蓄过剩到支出过剩，这个提炼方式太精辟了。这话太对了。而那个储蓄过剩也不过就是五年前的事。我们转变的速度真是惊人。 Chris Hussey 08:04 好的。发生的事情很多。你刚刚都跟我们说了。我们收个尾吧。现在这笔交易怎么做？ Rich Privorotsky 08:10 局面有点乱，而且我得说信心并不是特别高，但我认为电气化领域有一些板块我们认为看起来很有意思。它们的估值已经大幅下调，而且我仍然认为 A27 的能见度还很充足，能给你很大的安全边际。我认为有大量的航空航天资产已经回调，特别是在民用航空那一侧，同样对我们来说极具吸引力。然后甚至运输板块的部分领域，坦白说，如果能源问题能以某种方式解决，考虑到净头寸已经变得这么低、过去几周我们看到的抛售这么多，这笔交易里有很大的，我会说，凸性。举个例子，上周我们主经纪商业务中的科技股卖盘是有史以来最大的一次。所以，我认为有充足的理由保持担忧，我不想过度轻视这些风险，但我还是倾向于在目前这个时点保持谨慎乐观。好的，里奇，让我们快进到下周。下周有哪些会影响市场的事情是你在关注的？我认为关键在那些数字，也就是我们讨论过的超大规模云厂商的数字。我认为，你知道，让我们看看变现情况，让我们看看资本开支的数字。我认为这对盘面来说会非常关键。而且我认为，你知道，这件事的进展会决定人们对信贷的看法、对潜在需求的看法，以及我们从各家实验室和供应商那里得到的其他数据点。里奇，每次都带来大量信息。非常感谢你今天来做客。谢谢。那。 articles.title: 远期需求旺盛！亚马逊AWS今明年产能都已被抢空，连2028年的算力都快没了
articles.summary: 亚马逊的云计算部门正面临前所未有的市场需求，其绝大部分核心基础设施产能已在未来数年内被抢购一空。 亚马逊首席执行官Andy Jassy最新表态称， Amazon Web Services（AWS）的大部分产能已预订至2028年。 这一动态突显了企业端对云服务和人工智能基础设施持续且强劲的投资意愿。 尽管远期订单激增，亚马逊在资本支出层面依然保持了高度的运作弹性。公司能够根据客户需求的变化在短周期内调整服务器和网络设备的采购计划，这一防御性机制有效缓解了投资者对于云服务商过度扩产或未来需求放缓可能引发产能过剩的担忧。 除算力供需状况外，内部硬件生态的深化正在成为亚马逊应对市场需求的关键支撑。早期的战略性收购与近期对外部人工智能初创公司的投资正在形成协同效应，持续推动其自研芯片战略向前发展。 远期算力需求旺盛，核心服务预留弹性空间 在一档于周五发布的Andreessen Horowitz播客节目中，Jassy详细阐述了AWS目前的产能预订情况。他指出，随着企业对计算资源的需求不断攀升，AWS未来几年的大额产能已经基本见顶。 “现阶段2026年的产能显然已经售罄，2027年也已基本售罄。”Jassy在播客中表示，“2028年的很大一部分也已经售罄。” 尽管大块产能已被提前锁定，AWS并未完全切断短期需求的供给。Jassy补充说明，亚马逊始终会为按需服务以及运行应用程序的EC2和运行AI模型的推理服务Bedrock保留一定数量的算力，以确保核心服务的正常运转与客户体验。 资本开支具备防御性，按需调整硬件采购 针对市场周期波动可能带来的风险，亚马逊在数据中心硬件投入上采取了更为灵活的策略。即使未来整体算力需求增速出现放缓，亚马逊现有的供应链管理模式也能有效应对。 Jassy强调，AWS通常只需要提前几个月采购服务器和网络设备。这种较短的采购周期使得公司能够紧密贴合客户的实际需求来调整资本开支，避免了重资产投入带来的滞后风险。 “如果最终事实证明你不需要那么多产能来填满这些数据中心，你就不会去购买相关的服务器和网络设备，”Jassy明确表示。这种按需采购的逻辑为亚马逊的利润率和现金流提供了直接的保护。 自研芯片战略深化，合作提振技术能力 在讨论产能的同时，Jassy在广泛的采访中重点提及了亚马逊在底层硬件领域的长期布局。 他将十多年前对芯片制造商Annapurna Labs的收购，评价为可能是亚马逊有史以来最好的一笔收购交易。 Annapurna Labs目前是亚马逊内部自研芯片项目的核心驱动力，负责研发包括人工智能芯片Trainium和CPU处理器Graviton在内的关键硬件产品。这些自研硬件不仅降低了AWS对外部供应商的依赖，也为客户提供了更具成本效益的计算选项。 此外，生态合作正在反哺亚马逊的硬件开发。Jassy指出，亚马逊对人工智能初创公司Anthropic的投资对自身的芯片制造业务起到了积极的推动作用。 “[Anthropic]在Trainium上进行开发已经有一段时间了，我认为这对Anthropic非常有利，同时对我们的Trainium团队也非常有利，”Jassy表示，“我们从彼此身上学到了很多东西。” 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 38美元，DeepSeek算了一笔赚钱的账
articles.summary: 10月20日，DeepSeek开源推理框架DeepInfer时，公布了一个十分吸引眼球的数字：单个集群每天可以处理155万亿Token，如果按照DeepSeek API的谷时价格计算，平均每GPU小时对应38美元的收入。 这是根据Token处理量和公开API价格折算出的 理论计费收入 ，实际情况要复杂得多。但这个数字依然太有吸引力：如果粗暴按照线性外推，按每天24小时、全年365天计算，一张GPU的年化计费产值超过33万美元。 过去几年，AI行业一直在讨论训练一个前沿模型需要多少钱，英伟达的GPU有多贵，云厂商又投入了多少资金建设数据中心。但这些昂贵的计算设备买回来之后，究竟能够生产多少可以卖钱的智能？抛开眼花缭乱的“金融手段”，企业真能赚到的，又有多少钱？ DeepSeek的38美元，提供了一个难得的观察窗口。在资本市场再次对AI巨额投入的回报提出质疑的时候，产业一线的反馈却很乐观。“业内”和“业外”，产生了巨大的分歧。 一位经营Token中转业务的创业者告诉腾讯科技， 最近几个月，中小企业的AI需求正在“全面暴涨” ， 他能从客户的实际使用情况中感受到这一变化 。今年七八月还只有少数公司在尝试的事情，如今同行已经普遍在做。一些原本有数据安全顾虑的企业也开始私有化部署模型。他也在认真考虑“扩产”。 另外一位AI应用领域的创业者态度也十分鲜明：“英伟达的股票，我还是会继续买。”他接触的B端企业正在加快引入Agent，从日常运营到客户服务，越来越多业务开始AI化。 但他也判断，中美AI市场短期内可能经历一个“小低谷”。此前模型突破、生产率提升和AI替代工作的消息不断推高市场预期，当资本市场开始要求AI在真金白银上交出成绩时，企业应用的实际成果可能还没有跟上，市场热情也会随之回落。 这或许正是当下AI产业面临的矛盾：一线需求正在增长，但从应用落地到形成足以支撑巨额算力投入的商业回报，中间还有一段距离。 DeepSeek的计算提供了另一个值得关注的信号，即使按照谷时价格，高度优化的推理系统仍然能够实现相当可观的单位GPU计费产值。 那么， 随着推理效率不断提高，如果有足够多的用户持续消耗Token，AI是否已经可以成为一门赚钱的生意？答案可能比想象中乐观，但也更复杂。 一张GPU，每小时38美元 DeepSeek在9月10日发布的V4.1 Flash中，已经披露了不少推理效率优化的技术细节。 按照官方技术报告，这款模型拥有5520亿总参数，采用混合专家（MoE）架构和新的Causal Encoder–Decoder设计，处理输入时约激活80亿参数，生成输出时约激活160亿参数。 模型针对长上下文和Agent场景优化了缓存结构。按照论文披露，全局KV Cache占用降低到上一代的约四分之一，长期保存的缓存占用减少到约八分之一。每Token的全局KV Cache约为890字节，支持最高100万Token上下文。 这些优化直接影响长上下文推理的显存占用、数据传输和服务成本。 10月20日开源的DeepInfer，进一步公开了DeepSeek如何将这些技术整合为大规模在线推理服务。 它集成了此前陆续开源的FlashMLA、DeepGEMM、DeepEP、TileKernels等组件，同时引入专家并行、推测解码、异步调度等机制。 图：DeepSeek在线推理系统示意图 DeepSeek在官方部署问答中重点介绍了三项工程原则：适配不同厂商的加速硬件，将Prefill与Decode分开部署，以及尽可能长期保留KV Cache，减少重复计算。 在生产环境中，Prefill可以部署在普通8卡服务器上，而Decode采用64至128卡超节点，通过大规模专家并行提高吞吐量。DeepSeek还提出将KV Cache保留72小时以上，以适应Agent反复调用相同上下文的需求。 这些优化的核心目标，是在满足延迟要求的前提下，让同样数量的GPU服务更多请求。 不过，这次开源并不意味着DeepSeek已经公开完整生产环境中的所有组件。 官方README文档指出，KV Cache系统、视觉编码与Prefill/Decode分离服务编排、跨数据并行副本的负载均衡等，仍需要外部补齐。部分组件与DeepSeek内部基础设施深度耦合，因此尚未完整开源。 DeepInfer目前也主要面向DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash。其他模型如果在MoE专家组织、注意力结构、数值精度或硬件配置上存在较大差异，很难直接照搬。 因此，38美元并不代表任何企业下载DeepInfer、部署一批GPU，就能获得同样的收入表现。DeepSeek也没有完整公开计算这项指标所需的集群硬件构成、成本账单、付费流量比例及收入确认方式。 但它至少说明，在特定模型与硬件条件下，推理工程优化能够显著提高计算设备的潜在计费产值。 低价出售Token，与一张GPU产生较高的计费收入，并不矛盾。 关键在于，一小时内究竟能够处理多少有效Token，以及有多少Token真正可以向客户收费。 如果推理可以赚钱，为什么模型公司还在亏损？ 如果推理效率已经可以做到如此程度，为什么一些大模型公司仍然需要不断融资，甚至持续亏损？ 一个重要原因是，训练前沿模型和出售推理服务，本来就是两笔不同的账。 2026年斯坦福大学《AI Index》引用研究机构Epoch AI的数据，估算了OpenAI和Anthropic在模型研发与推理服务方面的计算支出。 2025年，OpenAI计算支出约163亿美元，其中研发相关计算支出83亿美元，推理支出80亿美元，两者几乎各占一半。 2024年，OpenAI的相应支出分别为40亿美元和18亿美元。 也就是说，一年之间，推理计算支出增长了约3.4倍，而研发计算支出增长约一倍。 Anthropic在2025年的计算支出估计为68亿美元，其中研发相关支出41亿美元，推理支出27亿美元。研发仍然占据较大比例。 这些数字说明，前沿模型公司的算力投入结构正在变化。随着商业用户增加，推理已成为越来越重要的成本来源，但研发开支并没有因为推理业务扩张而消失。 一家追逐SOTA的模型公司， 需要同时承担持续训练和大规模推理服务的成本 。前者包括预训练、后训练、强化学习、数据处理、模型评测及大量实验，后者则需要维持在线服务的算力、容量和稳定性。 Epoch AI特别指出，研发计算支出并不全部用于最后一次正式训练。 大量资源实际上消耗在实验、研究和模型迭代过程中 。因此，某个模型公开的单次训练成本，不能简单视为一家前沿模型公司的全部研发成本。 图源：Stanford HAI / Epoch AI，2026年 商业化带来的另一层压力，是用户越多，推理成本也可能越高。 《The Information》今年2月报道，OpenAI在2025年的毛利率约为33%，低于2024年的40%，也低于此前46%的预测。Anthropic对2025年毛利率的预期约为40%，虽然较2024年的负毛利状态改善明显，仍比其早先目标低10个百分点。 报道指出，两家公司毛利率低于预期的重要原因之一， 是实际推理成本高于原先估计。 这与DeepSeek的38美元看起来形成了矛盾：一边是持续改善的推理效率，另一边却是被推理成本侵蚀的毛利率。 实际上，它们反映的是同一门生意的两个方面。 单位GPU能够生产多少Token，是供给效率；公司需要投入多少GPU，才能满足不同客户的延迟、上下文长度、稳定性和峰值需求，则决定实际经营成本。 即使单位Token成本下降，重度用户增加、任务执行时间延长、模型调用次数上升，也可能使总推理支出迅速增长。尤其在固定月费的产品中，客户支付的价格未必随着Token消耗同步增加。想想每天挖空心思发“重置卡”的Tibo。 图：OpenAI产品与平台负责人Tibo（Thibault Sottiaux）于10月11日在X平台连续发布有关Reset的动态，其中“Day 6 / Reset”获得约290万次浏览。 一家模型公司的推理服务可以拥有正毛利，整个公司却仍然因为持续研发、基础设施和经营投入而亏损。 反过来，如果不承担前沿模型训练，专门经营推理服务，生意的成本结构就完全不同。 不训练模型，只卖Token能不能赚钱？ AI产业链中已经出现一类与前沿模型实验室不同的公司。 它们不以训练最强的基础模型为核心业务，而是部署DeepSeek、Qwen、Llama等开放权重模型，通过多芯片集群、推理框架、模型优化和调度系统，向开发者与企业销售API调用、专属推理实例或私有化部署服务。 对于这些公司来说，模型本身未必需要从头研发，成本主要来自GPU采购或租赁、机房与电力、网络和存储、推理系统研发、模型适配，以及销售、运维和客户支持。 其中最关键的三个变量，是单位GPU产值、实际付费利用率和综合运营成本。 假设一家推理服务商每GPU小时的完全负担成本为10美元，而它能够以DeepSeek披露的38美元作为满负载计费产值的参考，那么理论上只要实现约26.3%的有效计费产出，便可以覆盖这10美元成本。 如果有效计费产出达到50%，收入相当于每小时19美元，扣除10美元后还剩9美元。 当然，这只是用于说明商业敏感性的假设。实际系统的吞吐量、并发和延迟具有复杂关系，低负载下的收入不一定与满负载表现呈线性变化。10美元也不是DeepSeek披露的真实成本，更不能将计算结果当作其实际毛利率。 但这种测算说明，推理系统效率足够高时，商业回报可能具有较大的空间。问题是，GPU本身并不便宜，购买或者租赁GPU，同样不意味着立即拥有稳定收入。 CoreWeave提供了一个可以对照的真实案例。 2026年第二季度，CoreWeave收入25.75亿美元，同比增长约112%，调整后EBITDA达到15.10亿美元，利润率为59%。 但在美国通用会计准则下，公司当季仍净亏损6.26亿美元。问题出在算力生意高昂的资产和资金成本上。CoreWeave需要投入大量资金采购GPU及配套设备，相关资产随着使用逐年折旧；同时，公司依靠债务融资支持扩张，还要承担高额利息。2026年第二季度，其折旧及摊销费用达到13.93亿美元，净利息支出高达6.4亿美元。 折旧反映的是已经购入的算力设备在使用期间逐步计入的成本，利息是为这些投资融资所付出的代价。即使GPU租赁带来了可观收入，这两项负担仍可能大幅压缩利润。 CoreWeave的财报也说明，算力利用率高、收入增长快，并不意味着经营算力就一定赚钱。 更复杂的是，推理算力并不是一个完全同质化的市场。 DeepSeek能够通过深度优化获得较高单位GPU产值，不意味着普通推理服务商可以用相同的硬件、相同的价格获得同样表现。 因此， 推理服务可能是一门具有可观毛利空间的生意，但它并不会自动成为高利润生意 。工程能力影响成本下限，客户需求和定价权决定收入上限，而资本成本影响最终能留下多少利润。 此外，推理市场还面临持续降价的压力。 DeepSeek降低单位Token成本之后，也在通过更低的API价格将一部分效率收益传递给用户。其他公司一旦采用更高效的算法和系统，也可能参与价格竞争。 推理效率提升创造的收益，最终未必全部留给卖Token的公司。 AI利润版图，谁能赚钱？ 从英伟达、台积电、SK海力士，到数据中心和云服务商，AI基础设施投资已经为部分上游企业带来了可观的收入和利润。 但对于经营推理服务的企业来说，设备买回来之后，仍然需要不断寻找客户和任务，才能持续创造收入。 目前，Coding是商业化最清晰的AI应用市场之一，但即使在这个付费意愿较强的领域，盈利也并不容易。 《The Information》披露，Cursor在截至2026年1月的季度中，毛利率一度为-23%；如果将免费用户的推理费用全部计入销售成本，毛利率约为-31%。虽然此后毛利率已经转正，但高昂的模型调用成本，仍是AI应用需要面对的问题。 消费应用的情况更加分化。10月12日，曾经的明星AI陪伴公司Character.AI申请破产保护。根据破产文件及公开报道，公司当时仍拥有约1200万月活用户，2026年8月收入达到530万美元，但每月经营亏损仍有800万至900万美元。 仅2026年前八个月，Character.AI就花费了5610万美元购买算力，占运营费用约45%。即使转向更便宜的GPU和开放权重模型，并削减人员开支，也未能实现盈利。法律诉讼和监管压力同样加剧了公司的困境。 但是，AI原生应用并非无法盈利。Midjourney创始人David Holz在今年3月接受《The Information》采访时表示，公司2023年收入已显著超过2亿美元，此后继续增长，并且保持盈利。 但它也不是所有AI应用的普遍样本。图像生成拥有相对明确的使用场景和付费价值，而全天候运行的个人Agent，可能需要持续调用模型、使用工具和重新规划任务，成本结构更加复杂。 从整体市场看，需求实际上正在快速增长。 Menlo Ventures在2026年9月发布的《State of Consumer AI》报告估计，全球消费者AI支出已达到400亿美元，是2025年120亿美元的三倍多。 但值得注意的是，美国成年人AI使用率只从2025年的61%上升到64%。消费者AI支出的高速增长，主要来自 已有用户使用得更深入，付费更多 。新增用户有限。 图：Menlo Ventures消费AI支出图 Menlo Ventures合伙人Amy Wu Martin指出， 今年令人意外的变化，是消费者AI市场在没有迎来大量新用户的情况下实现了三倍增长 。推动增长的，是重度用户将AI带入更多生活场景，并开始允许AI代表自己采取行动。 现在，更重要的是一个用户每天有多少任务交给AI，以及每项任务能够创造多少实际价值。这也是Personal Agent（PA）重新成为大厂和创业公司共同关注方向的原因之一。 最近推出的Duet、Dots、Muse、Grokbot以及一批独立创业公司的产品，虽然在入口、记忆、权限体系和执行方式上存在不同，但都在尝试扩大AI能够承接的个人任务范围。 如果Agent能够持续处理邮件、安排工作、操作软件、完成采购、协调不同服务，AI调用便可能从用户主动发起的短时会话，转向围绕实际任务展开的长流程执行。 Agent之间的协作，以及越来越多由机器直接发起的工具调用和服务请求，也可能进一步扩大推理消费市场。 不过，更多Token消耗本身并不代表商业成功。 一家PA公司如果每月向用户收取20美元，却需要花费30美元购买模型调用和其他服务，那么它可能帮助上游模型商扩大收入，自己却仍然无法盈利。 同样，模型越来越高效，也可能让过去需要大量Token的任务变得便宜。即使Agent数量大幅增长，市场总收入也不一定以相同比例增长。 模型公司希望扩大推理消费市场，应用公司希望以更低的推理成本完成任务，用户关心实际完成的工作值多少钱。 DeepSeek的38美元，展示了在特定条件下，高效率生产Token所具有的潜在收入能力。 过去几年，资本市场为AI投入了巨额资金，芯片、存储和算力基础设施率先从中受益。随着推理系统继续进步，模型公司和应用公司一直在面对另外一道更复杂的商业命题： 如果越来越多企业都能以更低的成本生产智能，谁能找到足够多愿意购买智能的客户？ 还有更难的问题：如果AI是一个新的时代，token承载的“智能”，要创造什么增量？AI Native的核心逻辑，还在一片混沌中等待。 本文来源： 腾讯科技 articles.summary: 2026年4月23日，宁德时代（证券代码：300750）股东宁波联创减持，持股比例从6.23%下降至4.96%。 宁波联创询价转让股份数量为5800万股，占公司总股本的1.27%；询价转让的价格为410.34元/股，交易金额238亿元。 如今，这一笔5800万股进入解禁期。截至昨日收盘，宁德时代股价为237.6元，以收盘价计算，公司市值为1.1万亿。在昨天较前一日大涨7.8%的基础上，当初参与接盘宁波联创股权的基金依然浮亏42%。 宁德时代过去半年，股价遭遇腰斩。虽然宁德时代昨日股价反弹，但有投资者指出，当一个赛道高增长逻辑不复存在，都会引起恐慌性抛售，每一次暴跌后的反弹，都是大机构乘机逃跑的机会。 UBS浮亏25亿 小摩浮亏近18亿 宁波联创这笔股权一共有30家投资机构接盘，其中，UBS AG认购60.44亿元，摩根大通（小摩）旗下J.P.Morgan Securitiesplc认购41.65亿元，国泰海通金融控股有限公司认购15.84亿元，承壹投资管理有限公司认购2亿，中信证券资产管理（香港）有限公司认购2亿元，Mirae Asset Securities认购1.44亿元； NomuraSingapore认购1亿元，法国巴黎银行认购7386万元，兴证全球基金管理有限公司认购28.35亿元，南方基金管理股份有限公司认购12.8亿元，广基金管理有限公司认购5.79亿元，华夏基金管理有限公司认购3.94亿元，博时基金管理有限公司认购3.82亿元； 汇添富基金管理股份有限公司认购1.68亿元，财通基金管理有限公司认购1.44亿，建信基金管理有限责任公司、嘉实基金管理有限公司分别认购1.31亿元，诺德基金管理有限公司认购9438万元，泰康资产管理有限责任公司认购15.63亿元，中国人民养老保险有限责任公司认购7.22亿元； 以昨日股价计算，UBS AG浮亏约25亿元，J.P.Morgan Securitiesplc浮亏17.5亿元，国泰海通金融控股有限公司浮亏6.6亿元，兴证全球基金管理有限公司浮亏11.9亿元，南方基金管理股份有限公司浮亏5.4亿，泰康资产管理有限责任公司浮亏6.56亿元。 第三季营收1652亿 净利212亿 财报显示，宁德时代2026年前三季营收4421亿，同比增长56%；净利为645亿，同比增长31.6%；扣非后净利为578.76亿，同比增长32.68%。 其中，宁德时代2026年第三季营收1652亿，较上年同期增长58.58%；净利212亿，同比增长14.5%；扣非后净利为188.6亿，同比增长14.86%。 宁德时代高管在解读财报时表示，第三季度单位盈利能力变化有几方面因素：首先是产品结构变化，一个季度的产品结构波动不代表长期方向；第二是消费税和出口退税的影响。宁德时代正与客户沟通，一起来分担相关影响，同时积极推动新技术和新产品的落地，降低对盈利能力的影响。 宁德时代还表示，三季度的存货金额变大是随着公司业务规模发展带来的，但近几个季度公司存货周转天数一直相对稳定，并没有销售不畅或出货不畅的情况，属于正常存货周转。从存货结构来看，增长的主要是发出商品，未来会逐渐体现为公司收入。在储能方面，公司也在从销售电芯和直流侧产品到提供交流侧和系统产品，产品结构和形态较过去更为丰富，但相应的交付和确认收入周期比之前有所延长。 半年前配售募资391亿港元 截至2026年9月30日，曾毓群旗下厦门瑞庭投资持股22.04%，香港中央结算有限公司持股17.3%，黄世霖持股为9.09%； 截至2026年9月30日，宁德时代股权结构 宁波联合创新新能源投资管理合伙企业（有限合伙）持股为4.89%，HKSCC NOMINEES LIMITED持股为4.72%，李平持股4.27%，中国工商银行股份有限公司－易方达创业板交易型开放式指数证券投资基金持股0.67%，富泰华工业（深圳）有限公司持股0.62%， 中国人寿保险股份有限公司－传统－普通保险产品－005L－CT001 沪持股0.57%，北京华鼎新动力股权投资基金（有限合伙）持股0.52%。 宁德时代2026年4月30日还进行配售，配售价为628.20港元，募资净额为391.1亿港元。 本文来源： 雷递 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: AI资本开支陷入两难：加速则现金流承压，减速则增长故事失守
articles.summary: AI投资叙事正面临自身逻辑的内在矛盾。市场对超大规模云计算厂商资本开支路径的判断，已从此前的"正面无论如何都赢"演变为当前的"两害相权"困境—— 加速则自由现金流承压，减速则需求前景存疑，两条路均指向AI相关资产遭到抛售。 追风交易台消息，10月23日，据野村证券跨资产策略Charlie McElligott报告中指出，过去一周，AI生态系统内的负面情绪催化剂接连涌现，叠加此前9月"智能体热"行情中积累的多头仓位，市场经历了大规模的被迫平仓。 仅在最剧烈的单日抛售中，野村监控的124个美股多空配对中，有47个出现逾3个标准差的单日波动，6个触及5个标准差以上的极端偏离。 此次震荡不仅冲击了AI核心概念股，更通过拥挤仓位的连锁平仓，向美债、汇率及大宗商品市场蔓延，触发了跨资产范围的系统性去杠杆。 下周市场将迎来超大规模厂商财报密集披露窗口，包括谷歌、亚马逊、微软，叠加美联储议息会议，市场方向将在短期内面临关键检验。 资本开支的"囚徒困境" AI交易的核心叙事，已从此前"正面结果全面利好"的单边逻辑，急剧切换至"怎么看都是利空"的双向困境。 McElligott在报告中将这一处境描述为"任选其一都是毒药"： 其一，若超大规模厂商资本开支继续加速 。正如Meta最新财报所揭示的趋势， 市场将高度聚焦于自由现金流的持续消耗，并进一步质疑整体融资可持续性。 这一路径具有非线性风险，意味着需以更大规模、更高利差发行债务，AI交易因"不可持续"叙事而承压。 其二，若超大规模厂商资本开支出现实质性减速 ，则意味着市场此前已定价的"最优情景"， 涵盖AI需求、技术采用、盈利能力及终端用户生产率提升等核心论题正在失守，AI交易将面临更为猛烈的冲击。 这一困局的形成，与9月"智能体概念"行情期间多头仓位的快速重建高度相关。彼时大量资金涌入AI核心标的，并伴随着规模可观的看涨期权投机性建仓，为后续的踩踏式出逃埋下伏笔。 止损触发引发跨市场去杠杆 仓位拥挤是本轮波动异常剧烈的核心原因。 据野村交易台数据显示，在最剧烈的单日抛售中，共有124个美股多空配对触发止损，其中47个配对的波动幅度超过正负3个标准差，26个配对超过正负4个标准差，6个配对超过正负5个标准差。 （各类配对交易过去一段时间表现） McElligott认为，本轮止损潮的根源在于，2026年全年"高夏普比率交易"高度集中，套息策略与趋势跟踪策略长期共振，形成罕见的广谱赢家效应。 而当前时点恰逢四季度末，基金经理面临年末业绩压力，在已然承压的回撤环境下，主动出击博取反弹的动力远不及"保住资本、安全越年"的避险本能——"去风险、关仓位"模式主导了市场行为。 与此同时，AI叙事的重置正在加速系统性趋势策略的仓位调整，尤其集中于此前极为拥挤的美国国债及短期利率空头。 据野村QIS数据，过去两周，CTA趋势策略已平仓约680亿美元的美债期货空头及380亿美元的短期利率期货空头，但信号仍处于净空头状态，意味着若债市涨势延续，潜在的被迫回补规模依然可观。 （过去两周CTA已完成超千亿美元的空头回补，若要触发绿色框内下一波约500亿美元的强力追买，需等待债券价格进一步向上突破+2%的触发门槛） McElligott认为，随着短期窗口的回补基本完成，债券空头的挤压动能正在阶段性停歇。2周及1个月周期模型均已翻转为"做多"信号，但3个月周期模型若要从当前水平翻转做多，仍需债券价格出现大幅进一步上涨。 宏观共振：债券与股市的相关性切换 此次AI叙事重置，同步触发了债市与股市内部的相关性结构变化，这一信号在市场机制层面值得关注。 债券方面，"股债负相关"保护属性重新显现。 McElligott指出，大量资金于前一交易日通过股票期货抛售与国债期货买入完成资产配置切换，债券再度扮演风险对冲工具的角色。 这一特征贯穿全年的大部分时间后曾一度失效，如今伴随"增长恐慌"情景的信用度上升而回归。 股票市场则出现方向相反的切换。 2026年大部分时间内，纳斯达克及半导体板块呈现罕见的"上涨日波动率高于下跌日"特征；而当前，这一关系已重新反转为"负向现货-波动率相关性"，即股价下跌时波动率更大。 这一切换在纳斯达克及SMH（半导体ETF）空间最为突出，直接反映了市场对AI资本开支可持续性的重新定价。 （纳斯达克和半导体ETF指数在“下跌日”的成交量是“上涨日”成交量的近2:1，这一现象在10月份再度显现） 值得注意的是，标普500整体指数层面的VIX波动相对温和。McElligott将此归因于"反向离散"效应—— 科技多头遭受重创，而利率敏感型板块及其他空头标的则急剧反弹，两相对冲使得指数层面的整体相关性并未爆发式上升。 大额期权信号：逆势资金仍在布局AI反弹 尽管整体情绪承压，期权市场中仍出现了若干值得关注的逆势布局信号，主要体现在部分核心AI名称的看涨期权上。 据McElligott的观察，过去一周内出现了以下显著的看涨期权买入活动： CoreWeave合计支付权利金约6900万美元，涉及期权名义敞口约1.7亿美元； Nebius Group合计支付权利金约2570万美元，涉及名义敞口约8000万美元； 美光合计支付权利金约2000万美元，涉及名义敞口约8500万美元。 上述交易涉及2025年3月至4月到期的价外看涨期权，显示出部分资金在当前动荡中仍维持对AI板块中期反弹的方向性押注。 对于潜在的企稳条件，McElligott认为关键在于波动率风险溢价（VRP）卖方是否愿意遵循历史规律"逢波动率上涨做空"，尤其是0DTE Gamma卖出策略在买入下跌、卖出上涨方面的稳定器作用，将是判断波动率能否再度收敛的重要观察指标。 （0DTE伽马区间） articles.title: 恒大清盘新进展：毕加索、莫奈等名画被胡乱堆在原总部储物室，上百件艺术品亏本出售；广州还停着一架私人飞机，预计四季度收回1200万美元
articles.summary: 中国恒大的清盘又出现新进展。 《每日经济新闻》记者获悉，10月22日，中国恒大集团（清盘中）清盘人（以下简称恒大清盘人）发布了第二份进展报告，披露了自2025年8月1日至2026年9月30日期间清盘工作的重大进展。 报告显示，截至2026年9月30日，恒大清盘人已从集团资产中累计回收约34亿港元（约4.359亿美元），包括毕加索、莫奈等名家画作在内的一批“非典型资产”陆续亏本出手；与此同时，恒大清盘人已收到200份债权证明，主张的债权总额约3600亿港元（约460亿美元）。 恒大清盘人表示，目标是在2027年上半年宣派首次中期债款摊还，但具体的摊还债款比率未定，并称“将继续致力透过资产变现、追讨行动及法律程序，为债权人争取最大程度的回收款项，同时推进索赔判定工作”。 毕加索、莫奈名画等艺术品亏本出售 向美国一所大学追讨200万美元 在资产变现清单中，恒大曾经的艺术品收藏格外引人注目。恒大清盘人在恒大位于香港的原总部发现了上百件艺术品——没有妥善包装，也没存放在恒温恒湿的环境里，这些艺术品就这么被仓促地、胡乱地堆进一间储物室里面。 这批艺术品中包括毕加索、莫奈、安迪·沃霍尔等名家的作品，随便拿出一件，都是能在拍卖行挂上号的。恒大一家附属公司从2016年3月起的约18个月内陆续买入了这批艺术品，总成本约13亿港元。110件里，有95件从香港同一家艺术品经销商买入。 目前，恒大清盘人接管的107件艺术品已经通过苏富比卖出去96件，净收回2.25亿港元。整体而言，该批艺术品的出售价格低于其购入成本，因而录得亏损。 恒大清盘人称，尚未能完全确定恒大为何购入如此高价值及规模庞大的艺术品收藏，而此举并非公司日常业务的一部分。恒大清盘人了解到，购入该批艺术品至少部分是为了在恒大总部的一所“会所”内展示。 比名画更难出手的，是一架停在广州的私人飞机空客A319。报告显示，这架飞机自2023年起已不具备适航条件，且拖欠超过5000万港元的管理费及相关费用。恒大清盘人已经找到一位有意向接盘的买家，预计在今年四季度完成交易，净收回约1200万美元。 另外，恒大清盘人核查账目时发现，恒大账面有一笔约1.11亿港元（约1430万美元）的预付款。2020年2月，恒大、广州呼吸健康研究院与美国一所大学签署意向书，计划组建联合科研工作组，恒大同意预付这笔资金，用于相关科研项目。截至2021年7月，其中约1110万美元已动用，剩余320万美元未使用。清盘人经分析并取得法律意见后认为，恒大有权要求退回其中200万美元预付款，已向该校发函催款，目前双方正在协商和解。 从过往公开信息来看，上述美国大学应为哈佛大学。 已收总额约460亿美元债权索偿 目前尚未对索偿债权完成判定 报告披露，截至2026年9月30日，恒大清盘人共收到200份债权证明，主张债权总额约3600亿港元（约460亿美元）。恒大清盘人强调，该数字并非最终数字——目前尚未有任何一份债权证明表完成判定，且不排除仍有人继续提交债权申报索赔。 从目前申请的债权证明结构看，票据及债券约占债权总值的40%，内地金融机构的债权约占24%，集团内公司间余额约占22%，三类合计超过85%。恒大清盘人表示，已就收到的申索展开正式判定程序。基于有关索赔的性质及复杂程度，清盘人预计判定程序至少需时数个月方可完成。 报告称，透过恒大内地附属公司所持资产取得回收的可能性极低，恒大对内地项目的投资主要透过股权持有而非股东贷款的形式进行。目前，恒大在内地逾3000家境内实体中，已有超过650家进入破产程序。内地项目公司持有的资产已遭强制执行，并透过境内拍卖出售，拍卖所得的任何款项将首先用于清偿相关项目公司债权人的申索。 继广州市凯隆置业有限公司（以下简称凯隆置业，恒大地产的股东）启动破产管理程序后，恒大清盘人已向凯隆置业的破产管理人提出约14亿港元的索赔。 值得一提的是，报告还提到，恒大集团前CEO（首席执行官）夏海钧已于2022年迁往美国，其最初完全拒绝披露其资产，后在初步资产披露时又主动隐瞒其在美国的居所及资产。 本文来源： 每日经济新闻 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 上周散户“创纪录”抄底美国芯片杠杆ETF，本周跌爆了
articles.summary: 散户押注芯片股反弹的豪赌，以惨败收场。 上周，投资者向一只高风险半导体杠杆ETF单周注入创纪录的61亿美元，试图抄底持续下跌的芯片股。然而，这笔赌注几乎在入场的同时便开始亏损——本周芯片股非但没有反弹，跌势反而进一步加剧。 Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF（SOXL）本周再跌10.8%，创下连续第三周下跌，10月以来累计跌幅已超过43%。 市场的核心压力来自人工智能投资回报的不确定性。 投资者开始质疑，科技巨头在AI基础设施上的激进支出能否持续兑现盈利预期，这一情绪令半导体板块承压。 周四，SOXL单日暴跌20.5%，创下自6月23日以来最大单日跌幅 ，而当日正是此前持续流入的资金踩踏出逃的节点。与此同时，美股三大指数周五全线收跌，标普500信息技术板块录得自3月以来最长连跌周期——连续三周下跌。 创纪录抄底：61亿美元单周涌入 据FactSet数据， Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF上周单周吸引61亿美元资金流入，创历史纪录。 该ETF旨在提供追踪半导体指数日涨跌幅300%的放大收益，是市场上风险最高的杠杆工具之一。 这一创纪录的流入，发生在芯片股已连续下跌、AI交易情绪明显降温的背景下。投资者的逻辑是：跌得越多，反弹空间越大。FactSet数据显示，资金持续流入直至周四——而正是在周四，该ETF遭遇了单日20.5%的重挫。换言之， 抄底资金几乎精准踩在了加速下跌的节点上。 相比之下，非杠杆的iShares Semiconductor ETF同日跌幅为6.8%，损失虽同样可观，但远不及杠杆产品惨烈。 AI叙事遭遇质疑：芯片股估值承压 半导体股票今年以来涨幅惊人，iShares Semiconductor ETF年内一度飙升近59%，核心驱动力正是AI芯片需求的爆发式增长。然而，随着市场对AI基础设施投资回报的审视日趋严格，这一涨势正面临考验。 财富管理公司Glenmede投资策略副总裁Mike Reynolds表示，“半导体对AI基础设施建设极为敏感，而AI交易目前正受到一定程度的质疑。” 他同时指出， 在经历如此激进的涨势、估值已大幅抬升之后，投资者重新审视AI主题的潜在回报，是一种健康的市场行为。 “在市场达到彻底脱离基本面的狂热顶点之前，投资者能够实时提出质疑，这是好事，”Reynolds说。 杠杆ETF的双刃剑：放大收益，也放大风险 SOXL的遭遇，再次揭示了杠杆ETF作为投机工具的极端风险。这类产品通过衍生品实现每日收益的倍数放大，在市场单边上涨时可带来丰厚回报，但一旦方向判断失误，亏损同样成倍放大。 10月以来，SOXL累计跌幅已超过43%，而同期iShares Semiconductor ETF的月度跌幅约为15.9%。 两者之间的差距，直观呈现了3倍杠杆在下行市场中的破坏力。 芯片股的剧烈波动，本月已多次左右标普500指数的单日表现，令整个市场的情绪随之起伏。对于那些以杠杆ETF押注短期反弹的投资者而言，这场“抄底”的代价，远比预想中沉重。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
